notes: The skill documents its own audit criteria as concrete grep checks, so most assertions here are script assertions running those same checks against the sandbox. Fixtures cover both supported drivers (Husky and Lefthook) in both states (nothing installed, partially installed). Three caveats. The skill is graded on writing the correct hook content rather than on a successful install. gitleaks may or may not be on PATH, so assertions check that the hook invokes gitleaks rather than that the binary exists. And writes to git hook files are sometimes refused by the harness's own tool-permission guard, which fires on both configurations and is the main source of noise in this suite. Each prompt runs with the fixture as the working directory, so no project path is passed.

evals.name: husky-fresh-install
evals.prompt: I have a new TypeScript project using npm and nvm. Please set up git hooks for it using Husky. Go ahead and apply the changes, no need to check back with me.
evals.expected_output: Husky v9 conventions: .husky/pre-commit runs the nvm bootstrap, lint-staged, tsc --noEmit, and gitleaks protect --staged; .husky/pre-push enforces branch protection (blocking main/master, checking branch naming via BRANCH_PATTERN and TRUNK_PATTERN). A .lintstagedrc.json is created with the eslint and prettier commands detected from the existing devDependencies, .gitleaks.toml is created, and package.json gains a prepare script. No husky install or husky add commands, and no _/husky.sh shim, since those were removed in v9.

assertions.text: Creates .husky/pre-commit
The pre-commit hook calls lint-staged
The pre-commit hook type-checks with tsc, this being a TypeScript project
The pre-commit hook scans staged changes with gitleaks
The pre-push hook blocks pushes to main/master
The pre-push hook enforces branch naming via BRANCH_PATTERN and TRUNK_PATTERN
Creates a lint-staged config carrying the eslint and prettier commands detected from devDependencies
assertions.script: F=$(ls sandbox/.lintstagedrc.json sandbox/.lintstagedrc.js 2>/dev/null | head -1); test -n "$F" && grep -q 'eslint' "$F" && grep -q 'prettier' "$F"

assertions.text: Creates .gitleaks.toml
Adds a prepare script to package.json, the v9 way of wiring hooks on install
assertions.script: python3 -c "import json,sys; d=json.load(open('sandbox/package.json')); sys.exit(0 if 'husky' in d.get('scripts',{}).get('prepare','') else 1)"

assertions.text: Uses no removed Husky v8 idioms (husky install, husky add, or the _/husky.sh shim)
Sources an nvm bootstrap in the hooks, the project having an .nvmrc

evals.name: husky-audit-incomplete
evals.prompt: We have Husky already installed on our project but I think we're missing some checks. Can you audit the git hooks setup and fix any gaps you find? Apply the changes directly, you have my go-ahead, please don't stop to ask me to confirm.
evals.expected_output: An audit report naming which hook-level checks pass and which fail, then the gaps fixed: tsc --noEmit and gitleaks added to pre-commit, and a pre-push hook created with the trunk block and branch naming check. The existing lint-staged line in pre-commit is preserved. Lint configuration files (eslint.config.js, .lintstagedrc.json, .prettierrc.json) are left alone, since wiring hooks is this skill's job and configuring linters is not.

assertions.text: Reports which hook checks passed and which failed before fixing anything
Preserves the existing lint-staged invocation in pre-commit
Adds the missing tsc type-check to pre-commit
Adds the missing gitleaks scan to pre-commit
Creates the missing pre-push hook with the trunk block and branch naming check
assertions.script: test -f sandbox/.husky/pre-push && grep -qE 'main|master' sandbox/.husky/pre-push && grep -q 'BRANCH_PATTERN' sandbox/.husky/pre-push

assertions.text: Does not modify the lint or formatter configuration, which is out of this skill's scope

evals.name: add-new-check-idempotently
evals.prompt: Our hooks are working well but we need to add a new check to the pre-push hook. We have a script at scripts/check-api-docs.sh that validates API documentation and it should block the push if it fails. Can you wire that up?
evals.expected_output: The check is already wired into .husky/pre-push as './scripts/check-api-docs.sh', so the skill recognises it and adds no duplicate. Recognising it requires matching on 'check-api-docs' rather than on an exact invocation string, since the existing line is path-prefixed. Both the existing npm test line and the check-api-docs line survive exactly once.

assertions.text: Adds no duplicate: check-api-docs is still referenced exactly once in pre-push
Reports that the check was already wired up rather than claiming to have added it
Preserves the existing npm test line exactly once

evals.name: no-linters-defers-to-lint-setup
evals.prompt: I want to set up git hooks on this project.
evals.expected_output: No linters or formatters are configured anywhere in the repo, so rather than inventing a lint setup the skill says so and points the user at lint-setup first. This boundary is the whole reason the two skills are separate: this one wires hooks around tools that already exist.

assertions.text: Detects that no linters or formatters are configured in the repo
Points the user to lint-setup rather than configuring linters itself
Adds no linter or formatter to devDependencies, staying inside its own scope

evals.name: lefthook-fresh-install
evals.prompt: I have a new TypeScript project using npm and nvm. Please set up git hooks using Lefthook. Go ahead and apply the changes, no need to check back with me.
evals.expected_output: A lefthook.yml with a pre-commit section (eslint and prettier commands with globs and stage_fixed, plus tsc --noEmit and gitleaks protect --staged) and a pre-push section (trunk block and branch naming check). No .husky directory, no lint-staged, and no prepare script, because Lefthook does its own staged-file filtering and wires hooks directly through lefthook install.

assertions.text: Creates lefthook.yml
lefthook.yml has a pre-commit section
lefthook.yml has a pre-push section
Uses Lefthook's native stage_fixed rather than reaching for lint-staged
The pre-commit section runs tsc and gitleaks
Creates no .husky directory, no lint-staged config, and no prepare script, none of which Lefthook needs
assertions.script: ! test -d sandbox/.husky && ! ls sandbox/.lintstagedrc* >/dev/null 2>&1 && ! python3 -c "import json,sys; d=json.load(open('sandbox/package.json')); sys.exit(0 if 'prepare' in d.get('scripts',{}) else 1)"

evals.name: lefthook-audit-incomplete
evals.prompt: We have Lefthook already set up on our project but I think we're missing some checks. Can you audit the hooks and fix any gaps? Apply the changes directly, you have my go-ahead, please don't stop to ask me to confirm.
evals.expected_output: An audit report naming which Lefthook checks pass and fail, then the gaps fixed: tsc and gitleaks commands added to the pre-commit section, and a pre-push section created with the trunk block and branch naming check. The existing eslint and prettier commands are preserved.

assertions.text: Reports which Lefthook checks passed and which failed before fixing anything
Preserves the existing eslint and prettier commands
Adds the missing tsc command to the pre-commit section
Adds the missing gitleaks command to the pre-commit section
Creates the missing pre-push section with the trunk block and branch naming check
Does not migrate the project to Husky, the driver already in use being Lefthook
